[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Application Security Testing — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise MAY employ an architectural capability to instrument running application instances to monitor internal behavior during test execution, producing higher-fidelity vulnerability findings by correlating external stimulus with internal code execution paths.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to instrument application runtime and observe internal data flows during functional or security test execution
- Correlation of observed internal behavior with vulnerability patterns
- Findings reporting integrated with existing AppSec testing output channels

**Out of Scope**:
- Source code analysis without execution (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07)
- Black-box external probing without instrumentation (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08)
- Runtime protection in production (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RASP-2.7.20)
- Security controls, tool selection, or configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- IAST instrumentation SHALL be used in test environments only and SHALL NOT be deployed to production systems.
- IAST findings SHOULD be correlated with SAST findings to reduce false positives and confirm exploitability.
- The overhead introduced by IAST instrumentation SHOULD be evaluated before inclusion in time-sensitive pipeline stages.
- IAST is an optional layer of the testing posture; organizations SHOULD assess its value relative to SAST+DAST coverage before adoption.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09.md#runtime-instrumentation]

#### Runtime Instrumentation

**Architectural intent**: Observe application-internal data flows during test execution to identify vulnerability patterns that are not visible from source code analysis or external probing alone.

**Design guidance**:
- Instrumentation SHALL be applied only to application processes in designated test environments.
- The instrumentation mechanism SHOULD NOT require changes to application source code.
- Performance impact of instrumentation SHALL be characterized and documented before pipeline integration.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09.md#finding-correlation]

#### Finding Correlation

**Architectural intent**: Reduce finding noise by confirming that externally triggered inputs reach vulnerable internal code paths.

**Design guidance**:
- IAST findings SHOULD be exported in the same format as SAST and DAST findings to enable unified tracking.
- Confirmed vulnerabilities (where external trigger + internal execution path are both observed) SHOULD be escalated above unconfirmed findings in triage prioritization.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Test Execution Trigger | Inbound | Functional/Security Test Suite | Test traffic that exercises application paths under instrumentation |
| Runtime Agent | Bidirectional | Application Process | In-process agent that observes and reports internal behavior |
| Findings Output | Outbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06 | Structured findings correlated with test execution |
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

IAST advances the Applications and Workloads pillar by providing higher-confidence validation that application code paths cannot be exploited, reducing the risk that applications admitted to production environments carry confirmed vulnerabilities.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the SA family (security engineering in the SDLC) and the CA family (security assessments). The correlation capability specifically supports the intent of the SI family's flaw identification requirements.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- IAST requires language- and framework-compatible instrumentation agents; applicability varies by technology stack.
- IAST is most valuable when combined with comprehensive functional test coverage; low test coverage limits IAST's ability to exercise vulnerable code paths.
- Not all application architectures support IAST; this ABB is designated optional (MAY) accordingly.
